note.text: The simple present commonly expresses habits or general states; the simple past commonly presents a completed event in a past context. For a third-person singular present subject, ordinary verbs usually add -s or -es. Past negatives and questions with did use the base verb: did not go, not did not went. Be has its own forms. Time words guide interpretation but do not replace reading the meaning. Compare the present habit with the completed past event before choosing a form.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose between a present habit and a completed past event and form a past negative correctly. Builds on: parts of speech and the tense overview. Leads to: transitivity, future forms and later narrative tense contrasts.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: The simple present commonly expresses habits or general states; the simple past commonly presents a completed event in a past context. For a third-person singular present subject, ordinary verbs usually add -s or -es. Past negatives and questions with did use the base verb: did not go, not did not went. Be has its own forms. sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original contrast: Bih {thirdPerson('buy')} materials on market days. Yesterday she {past('buy')} an item. She did not buy it the day before. The negative uses did to carry the past; bought must not be added after did. In a habit report, yesterday cannot simply be attached to the present form without changing the intended construction.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the time frame and whether the sentence is affirmative, negative or a question. Check subject agreement in the present and irregular forms in the past. Preserve the meaning when correcting; do not add two past markers around did.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Every habitual sentence must be a past event. Correction: The simple present can report a repeated activity.
Yesterday Bih buy the item is the standard affirmative model. Correction: Use the simple past for the completed event in this model.
Bih did not bought the item is the standard model. Correction: Did carries the past; the following verb stays in the base form.
He choose is always the neutral school agreement pattern. Correction: The singular third-person subject requires the appropriate present form.

questions.prompt: Complete the finished past event: Yesterday Bih ___ the item. Base verb: {v}.

misconceptions.explain: The base form alone does not mark this affirmative completed past event.
That is a third-person present form, not the past required.
An -ing form alone is not a finite simple-past verb.

solution: The event is presented as completed yesterday.

e: After did use go.
The auxiliary and lexical form are wrong for this past negative.
An ordinary past negative needs did not in this model.
pick.y: Did not takes the base go.

pick.q: Correct the question about a past purchase.
e: Use buy after did.
This mixes present auxiliary with a past form.
Do not add third-person -s after did.
pick.y: Did carries the past in the question.

pick.q: Choose the ordinary present habit with she.
w: She read every evening, in the stated present habit.
e: The explicit present-habit context needs third-person agreement.
The phrase lacks a finite verb.
After do the ordinary form would be base; this is not the requested neutral habit pattern.
pick.y: She takes reads in this model.

pick.q: Choose the finished event in the stated past context.
e: That present singular form does not fit.
A finite verb is missing.
Did would take arrive, not arrived.
pick.y: Arrived is a finite simple-past form.
